survey: A stage spotlight hanging from a truss. The truss is a flat ladder: two parallel horizontal tubes joined by diagonal braces. It rises gently to the right and is seen slightly from below and in front, and its right end caps appear as small round discs. A block clamp grips the middle of the truss. A short vertical stem drops from the clamp to a U-shaped yoke, which is seen nearly face-on with its crossbar horizontal. The yoke's arms come down both sides of a cylindrical lamp housing and attach with round pivot knobs (the right knob is visible, the left one is hidden behind the can). The pivot axis runs left to right across the picture. The housing points down and to the left, toward the viewer, so the pivot axis is roughly perpendicular to it. We see the vented upper side of the housing and its round front face, which is drawn as a moderately foreshortened ellipse. That face holds three lenses (yellow, cyan, red), which are slightly oval to match it. The light beams leave along the housing's axis toward the lower left. The truss tubes stay parallel to each other. The stem is vertical and lines up with the clamp and the middle of the yoke. Every part reads as one consistent view from slightly below and in front.
